Order 
Vide this order, I shall decide whether or not there are sufficient grounds for proceeding against the respondent no.2 and summoning him as accused in the present complaint case.
2. Thumb nail sketch of the case of the complainant is that he is working as Sub Inspector (SI) with Delhi Police since 2010 and belongs to the 'Jatav' caste which is Scheduled Caste community.

Complainant was posted in Police Station Malviya Nagar from February 2017 to January 2020 where he met lady Ct M (identity not revealed herein and name and other details are mentioned in the complaint), wife of respondent no.2 who was posted in the same police station from 2018 to 2020 and Ms. M often told the complainant that her husband is of a paranoid/suspicious nature.
3. On 19.07.2021, Ms. M made a whats app call to complainant and told him that she was on duty at Police Station Hauz Khas and asked the complainant to drop her at Mahipalpur which was near to Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93763691/
1 her house as it was raining very heavily.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As Ms. M was getting out of the complainant's car around 07am, slightly ahead of Mahipalpur flyover, respondent no.2 saw her from the opposite side of the road and came near the complainant's car and started shouting at/scolding his wife that earlier also he had forbidden her when another constable had dropped her but he did not say much as that person was of the same caste but now she has come with the complainant who is a low caste and degenerate person.
4. Respondent no.2 then started hurling abuses at the complainant and made derogatory remarks against his caste.

Respondent no.2 used words as 'chamar' and 'lower caste' in a derogatory,
obnoxious and insulting manner in full public view.
Thereafter, respondent no.2 then ran towards the complainant with a stone in his hand stating that he would not spare this 'dedhchamar'.

Respondent no.2 was later stopped by members of the public who asked him not to humiliate the complainant in the name of his caste but the respondent no.2 further humiliated the complainant by telling everyone around him that in his village, low caste person like complainant were not even allowed to sit with upper caste and here such persons behave as equals.

5. Wife of respondent no.2 told the complainant to leave from the place as her husband bears hatred for Scheduled caste and she will try to make her husband understand and she requested the complainant not to file any complaint against him as it would put a wrong impression on her children.
With the intervention of public, complainant managed to save himself and leave that place and did not make any complaint against respondent no.2 keeping the request of Ms. M in mind.

6. On the intervening night of 28/29 July 2021 at around 02:30am, while the complainant was at Khirki, Malviya Nagar, he received a phone call on his mobile number 9871xxxxxx (mentioned in the complaint) from respondent no.2 (mobile no.7011xxxxxx) (mentioned in the complaint) and he hurled abuses at the complainant and made caste based remarks as 'chamar' and 'dedh' (lower caste) in a highly derogatory and insulting manner.

However, the complainant told respondent no.2 that he was with his acquaintances and due to some problem with his phone, the voice was not clearly audible and that complainant would have to put the phone on speaker mode.

Complainant requested respondent no.2 not to use such words as other could listen, but respondent no.2 did not stop and kept on making humiliating caste based remarks and abuses against the complainant.

7. Respondent no.2 dared the complainant to record the conversation if he wants and threatened that he will get the complainant shot from his wife and respondent no.2 threatened that within seven days, the complainant will be at his feet begging forgiveness.
8. Entire conversation was heard by Danish and Farhan who were friends of complainant and Danish recorded the same on his phone.

As threatened, respondent no.2 got a false first information report (FIR) registered at PS Malviya Nagar against the complainant on the basis of false allegations of rape.
9.

Wife of respondent no.2 also sent a message through a common acquaintance that she was pressurized by her husband to file the false complaint and she will talk to her husband about it and withdraw the complaint against the complainant and she again requested the complainant not to file Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93763691/
2 a complaint against her husband for the atrocities committed by him upon the complainant.

sentences.text: 10. Complainant was under extreme distress and shock due to this false FIR against him and was unable to think rationally as to what he should do and when the complainant was granted protection by the court, he got some reprieve from the extreme mental trauma and filed a formal complaint with SHO PS Malviya Nagar on 29.08.2021.
Copy of the complaint was also sent to the superior/senior police officials.

11. Despite complaint dated 29.08.2021 to SHO PS Malviya Nagar and also to senior police officials,
no action was taken by the police.
The complainant, accordingly, filed the present complaint case.
12. Action Taken Report dated 18.02.2022 was filed by ACP Hauz Khas.
However, vide order dated 04.03.2022, the application under section 156(3) Cr.P.C. of the complainant was dismissed and the matter was listed for pre-summoning evidence.

13. Complainant himself was examined as CW1, who reiterated the incident and marked correct transcription of recording as Ex.CW1/B, CD as Ex.CW1/C, complaints as Ex.CW1/D and Ex.CW1/E,
copy of case FIR no.467/2021 PS Malviya Nagar, under section 376/506 Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) as Ex.CW1/F, complaint given to DCP as Ex.CW1/G, copy of mail sent by complainant for registration of FIR as Mark CW1/H, complaint given to DCP, South District as Ex.CW1/J, complaint as Ex.CW1/H, affidavit as Ex.CW1/K, additional affidavit as Ex.CW1/L.
14.
Complainant also examined two more witnesses namely Sh. Farhan as CW2 and Sh. Danish as CW3.
CW3 marked one pen drive as Ex.CW3/A and certificates under section 65B of Indian Evidence Act as Ex.CW3/B and Ex.CW3/B-1.

sentences.text: Record further reveals that on 11.05.2023, it was noted that the report of ACP in terms of the order dated 14.03.2023 was received with annexures.
17. Post aforesaid proceeding, arguments on pre- summoning evidence were concluded.

Ld. Counsel for complainant recapitulated the factual matrix of the complaint and the evidence led by the complainant as to how the two incidents dated 19.07.2021 and 28-29.07.21 unfolded and the specific role of respondent no.2 in insulting the complainant by making derogatory remarks against his caste.

Ld. Counsel also assailed the inquiry report under section 202 Cr.P.C to the extent of terming it as biased and unreliable in some parts as the incident dated 19.07.2021 is stated to have occurred around 07am but the investigating officer chose to conveniently manipulate the facts and disclosed the location of the complainant and respondent no.2 at about 07:17am.
Ld. Counsel labored hard to assert that the alleged place of incident was not got physically verified from any independent witness.
18. I have meditated the records of the case and the arguments advanced.

19. Perusal of the testimony of complainant/CW1 reveals that he has been working as Sub Inspector with Delhi Police since 2010 and belongs to Jatav community which is a scheduled caste as demonstrated from his caste certificate Ex.CW1/A.

In his statement, he has spoken about an incident of 19.07.2021 that he received a call from Ct. M who was on duty at PS Hauz Khas and since it was raining heavily, she asked him to drop at her home after her duty hours and at about 06:15am,
Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93763691/
4 he picked her up from PS Hauz Khas and took her to Mahipalpur to drop her at her house in his car.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They reached there at around 07:00am and when she was getting out of his car, he noticed that her husband (respondent no.2) was present across the road.

CW1 further claimed that upon seeing them, her husband came near them after crossing the road and screamed on Manisha by stating "phele tu kisi aur Manoj naam ke sipahi ke sath aayi thi, per mene kuch nahi kaha kyuki wo yadav tha and said that aaj tu is chamar dhedh ke sath aayi hai, tujhe nahi chhodunga".
CW1 further alleged that after stating this, he picked up a stone and ran towards him and stated "chamar dhedh ko nahi chhodunga".
His statement further reveals that public persons gathered there and respondent no.2 was stopped from attacking the complainant/CW1.
Persons from the public tried to pacify and convince her husband as he used to hate the lower caste people.
She also requested not to take any action against her husband and, therefore, complainant/CW1 did not make any complaint at that time and due to intervention of the public persons, he left the place.
20. The aforesaid statement of the complainant and his non reporting of the aforesaid alleged incident do not inspire the confidence of this court for ensuing reasons:
As per the inquiry report under section 202 Cr.P.C, distance from the spot of the alleged incident and location of house of respondent no.2 was found to be approximately 01km.
This fact has not been oppugned on behalf of the complainant.

There is no reasonable explanation as to how respondent no.2 i.e. the husband of Ct.
M ended up standing on the road where complainant/CW1 has alleged to have dropped Ct. M at 07:00am.
There is no such deposition that Ct. M had informed her husband in advance that she was coming to her home and would reach around 07am.
It is unlikely that without any indication of reaching of Ct. M at her home, respondent no.2 would walk through 01 km distance to come at the road where Ct. M was dropped by the complainant.

Complainant has not tendered any site plan of the exact place where he dropped Ct.
M and where the respondent no.2 was found standing at the time of alleged incident.
Complainant has not examined any independent public persons who were alleged to have been gathered at the spot of the incident.

Considering the gravity of the situation, complainant being a police official himself, ought to have been diligent enough to inquire from the public persons gathered there and to join anyone of them as a witness in the present complaint.

Admittedly, complainant chose to not make any complaint in regard to the said incident soon thereafter and the reason put forth by him that Ct. M convinced him not to take any action against her husband does not appear to be plausible.

Rather,
the record reveals that the complainant lodged the first complaint to the SHO after a month of the alleged second incident of 28/29.07.2021 and after registration of FIR No.467 dated 03.08.2021 under section 376 IPC against him by Ct. M i.e. the wife of respondent no.2.
Thus, the filing of present complaint as a counter blast cannot be ruled out.

sentences.text:
In regard to the next incident on the intervening night of 28-29/07/2021, deposition of complainant/CW1 is reproduced as under:
".....Thereafter, in the intervening night of 28/29.07.2021 at about 2:30 AM when I was present Khirki, Malviya Nagar, when I received a call from Devender Yadav from mobile phone no. 7011949508 on my mobile phone no. 9871990051 and addressed me with casteist remarks such as chamar and dhedh and started abusing me.
After this, I told him that he was on speaker phone and he should not talk in such a manner as other people were also with me and I disconnected the phone.
I again received a call from him when I was present opposite Select City Walk Mall in the parking area in front of athletic gym.
Prior to this I called Danish who was having a saloon nearby as I wanted to stay at his house during that night.
He came in the parking lot along with his brother, namely, Farhan and both were present when I received the call from Devender Yadav.
He again started abusing me while the call was on speaker mode.
On my request, Danish started recording this call by using his mobile phone.

Devender Yadav abused me and stated "tere ko recording karni hai to karle, recording teri gand me de dunga aur tujhe apni patani se goli lagwaunga, 7 din ke andar agar mene goli nahi mari to mera naam nahi" etc.
These abuses and cast remarks were duly recorded in the mobile phone of Danish....."

22. The discernment of the aforesaid shows that the alleged casteist remarks were hurled at the complainant/CW1 over phone by respondent no.2, which the complainant/CW1 further postulates to have been heard by CW2 and CW3, both of whom were with him and his phone was on speaker.

The said Farhan has been examined as CW2 and Danish as CW3, both of whom have spoken on the lines of the deposition of the complainant/CW1 in regard to the incident of 28/29.07.2021.
23.

Before examining the legality of whether hurling of casteist remarks over phone would constitute an offence under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989)
(SC/ST Act

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: ), let us dissect the deposition of CW1 in regard to the incident of 28/29.07.2021 in the light of the inquiry report filed by ACP Harish Chander under section 202 Cr.P.C.

It is the claim of the complainant/CW1 that in the intervening night of 28/29.07.2021 at about 02:30am, when he was present at Khirki, Malviya Nagar, he received a call from respondent no.2 from mobile no.701194xxxx on his mobile phone no. 987199xxxx, addressing him with casteist remarks such as 'chamar' and 'dhedh' and also abused him.

Inquiry report under section 202 Cr.P.C unravels that on 29.07.2021 at 1:48:56, complainant called from his mobile number 9871xxxxxx to the respondent no. 2 on his mobile no.7011xxxxxx for 177 seconds.

Further, at 1:49:53, complainant called from his mobile number 9871xxxxxx to Ct. M on her mobile number 7011xxxxxx for 41 seconds and it is only after these calls, complainant received calls from respondent no.2.

It is clear from this that it was the complainant who initially called respondent no.2 and his wife Ct.
M perhaps to provoke them, particularly respondent no.2, and when respondent no.2 retorted,
complainant went on to put his phone on speaker mode and thereafter he also got joined Danish and Farhan so as to make out a case that the alleged casteist remarks were hurled by respondent no.2 within public view.

Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93763691/
6 24.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Complainant has also claimed to have recorded the mobile conversation between him and respondent no.2, which was also played in court, during arguments.

The entire recording and its transcript indicate that though respondent no.2 had used casteist remarks against the complainant,
but from the recording, it is culled out that it was the complainant who kept on provoking respondent no.2 by abusing him incessantly and respondent no.2 was retorting back.

From the sequence of the events, the entire incident of 28/29.07.2021 appears to be stage managed by the complainant/CW1 in order to create a cause of action in his favor so as to pin down respondent no.2 under SC/ST Act.

25. Now, if we analyze the afore referred incident in the light of legal wrangles which come in the way of attracting the offence under SC/ST Act, it is to be seen whether the uttering of any casteist remarks over phone would constitute an offence under SC/ST Act.

In this regard, reference can be made to the judgment of Punjab and Haryana High Court in case titled as Sandeep @ Deepa Vs.
State of Haryana and Another, dated 14.05.2020, CRR No.1574/2019 (O&M), the relevant portion is as under:
"To constitute the offence under the Act, it must be alleged that the accused intentionally insulted or intimidated with intention to humiliate a member of Scheduled Caste or Schedule Tribe in any public place within public view.

entities.text:
Sandeep @ Deepa Vs.
State of Haryana and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, it is alleged that the offence has been committed by the petitioners by using the caste based remarks over a mobile phone call to the informant, or a member of Scheduled Castes, of which there are no records.

Once it s admitted that the alleged conversation over the mobile phone was not in a public gaze nor witnessed by any third party, the alleged use of caste words cannot be said to have been committed within the public view.

The allegations against the petitioners-accused are that caste based remarks were made by them on mobile phone and when Devi Dayal along with other persons went to the petitioners asking them to respect respondent No. 2, who is a Sarpanch, at that moment the complainant was not present.....
Therefore, in view of the above, it is evident that the prosecution has failed to make out a prima facie case for commission of offence punishable under Section 3 of SC & ST Act.

Moreover, the basic ingredients of the offence in the FIR are that there must be intentional insult, secondly the insult must be done in a public place within public view, which is not in the present case.
Thus, the essential ingredients which must be fulfilled, are not found in the present case.
Since these are the penal provisions, the same are to be given a strict construction and if any of the ingredients are found lacking, it would not constitute the offence under the SC/ST Act."

26. In the light of the afore-noted judgment, the position is crystallized that the telephonic conversation involving casteist remarks which are not made in public gaze does not come within the purview of the public view.

Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93763691/
7 27.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this juncture, an observation of the High Court in the judgment of Pradeep Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (noted above) is worth noting that what if the alleged conversation over the mobile phone was in a public gaze or witnessed by any third party if the phone is on speaker mode and other persons are present who overhear the objectionable conversation, whether that would still not attract the offence under SC/ST Act.

entities.text: Pradeep Kumar Vs. State of Haryana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In my opinion, since the relevant provision i.e. section 3(1)(r)
of SC/ST Act speaks about the intention of the speaker to insult or intimidate, an element of mens rea assumes significance.

If the case is such that the speaker making casteist remarks over phone does not intend the same to be heard by any one other than the recipient of the same, the fact that the recipient by putting the phone on speaker mode wants the public persons to hear the conversation and to bring it within the ambit of 'public view', in that case the benefit of same must not enure to the recipient who can be said to be indulging in circumventing the law.

In the instant case, it is the deposition of the complainant/CW1 that initially, he told respondent no.2 that he was on speaker mode and that he should not talk in such a manner as other people were also with him,
but he disconnected the phone.

When he again received a call from respondent no.2, by that time,
he had already joined over his known persons namely CW2 Farhan and CW3 Danish and then he deliberately put his phone on speaker mode and recorded the conversation.
This, in my view, would be an act of subterfuge on the part of the complainant in order to trick the other side to fall in the trap.

Otherwise also, from the deposition of complainant/CW1, it is not made out that respondent no.2 was made aware that during his second call, the phone was put on speaker mode and that CW2 and CW3 were listening the conversation and, thus, there cannot be any intention on the part of the respondent no.2 to humiliate the complainant by hurling casteist remarks against him.
28.

In so far as Section 506 IPC is concerned, though, dehors the offence under SC/ST Act having been made out, the jurisdiction to inquire into the offence under section 506 IPC does not lie with this court, nevertheless, I am of the view that even if respondent no.2 stated to the complainant over phone 'tere ko recording karni hai to karle, recording teri gand me de dunga aur tujhe apni patani se goli lagwaunga, 7 din ke andar agar mene goli nahi mari to mera naam nahi', the pre requisite for the offence under section 506 IPC is not fulfilled as mere uttering of the threatening words is not enough for making out the offence as the threat should be serious, impending and real.

In the case of Manik Taneja and Another Vs. State of Karnataka and Another, dated 20.01.2015, 2015 AIR SCW 948, the Supreme Court had observed in paragraph 15 as under:
"In the instant case, the allegation is that the appellants have abused the complainant and obstructed the second respondent from discharging his public duties and spoiled the integrity of the second respondent.

entities.text: Manik Taneja and Another Vs. State of Karnataka and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the intention of the accused that has to be considered in deciding as to whether what he has stated comes within the meaning of "Criminal intimidation".
The threat must be with intention to cause alarm to the complainant to cause that person to do or omit to do any work.
Mere expression of any words without any intention to cause alarm would not be sufficient to bring in the application of this section.
But material has to be placed on record to show that the intention is to cause alarm to the complainant.

From the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that there was no intention on the part of the appellants to cause alarm in the minds of the second respondent causing obstruction in discharge of his duty....."

Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93763691/
8 29.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case in hand, from the recorded conversation Ex.CW1/C and the transcript Ex.CW1/B

, it can be deduced that the alleged words spoken by respondent no.2 were in retaliation to the expletives and abusive remarks made by the complainant to him and there cannot be said to be any intention to cause alarm to the complainant and those threats cannot be said to be real and imminent.
Thus, case of the complainant qua the offence under section 506 IPC also does not deserve to see the light of the day.

30. The reliance of Ld. counsel for the complainant on the judgment of Swaran Singh and Ors Vs.
State and Another, SLP Criminal No. 987/2008 is not of any assistance as the facts of the said case were distinct.

entities.text:
Swaran Singh and Ors Vs.
State and Another, SLP Criminal No. 987/2008
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The other two judgments in Shivji Singh Vs. Nagendra Tiwary and Others, SLP (Criminal) no.1416/2009 and Ghulam Hassan Beigh Vs. Mohammad Maqbook Magrey and Ors,
SLP (Criminal) No. 4599/2021 are on the general principle of making out of prima facie case, which is not the case herein in view of the foregoing discussion.

entities.text: Shivji Singh Vs. Nagendra Tiwary and Others, SLP (Criminal) no.1416/2009
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Ghulam Hassan Beigh Vs. Mohammad Maqbook Magrey and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, in so far as the argument that the ACP has not complied with the mandatory provision of Section 15A (10) of SC/ST Act, which mandates to make the video recording of all the proceedings, it is observed that this complaint was being proceeded as a private complaint and the inquiry ordered under section 202 Cr.P.C was on limited aspects, therefore, there was no requirement on the part of the concerned ACP to comply with the provision of Section 15A(10) of SC/ST Act.
31.
For the reasons aforesaid, there is no merit in the present complaint, and no case is made out to summon respondent no.2.
Hence, the complaint stands dismissed.
File be consigned to record room.

In so far as Section 506 IPC is concerned, though, dehors the offence under SC/ST Act having been made out, the jurisdiction to inquire into the offence under section 506 IPC does not lie with this court, nevertheless, I am of the view that even if respondent no.2 stated to the complainant over phone 'tere ko recording karni hai to karle, recording teri gand me de dunga aur tujhe apni patani se goli lagwaunga, 7 din ke andar agar mene goli nahi mari to mera naam nahi', the pre requisite for the offence under section 506 IPC is not fulfilled as mere uttering of the threatening words is not enough for making out the offence as the threat should be serious, impending and real.
Manoj Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93763691/
8 29.
In the case in hand, from the recorded conversation Ex.CW1/C and the transcript Ex.CW1/B
, it can be deduced that the alleged words spoken by respondent no.2 were in retaliation to the expletives and abusive remarks made by the complainant to him and there cannot be said to be any intention to cause alarm to the complainant and those threats cannot be said to be real and imminent.
Thus, case of the complainant qua the offence under section 506 IPC also does not deserve to see the light of the day.
